name: Ventral diencephalon
summary: The ventral diencephalon is the FreeSurfer segmentation label that groups the structures below the thalamus that are hard to separate on T1-weighted images: the hypothalamus, the mammillary bodies, the subthalamic nucleus, the zona incerta and fields of Forel, the substantia nigra and red nucleus at the diencephalic-midbrain junction, the optic tract, the ventral tegmental area and the geniculate region. It is used in this atlas as the container mesh for the hypothalamic and subthalamic nuclei that the higher-resolution atlases subdivide, and its volume is a crude but reproducible measure of the diencephalon in dementia and in hypothalamic disease.

anatomy.location: The tissue between the thalamus above and the interpeduncular cistern and cerebral peduncles below, from the optic chiasm and lamina terminalis in front to the posterior commissure and the midbrain behind, lateral to the third ventricle and medial to the internal capsule and the optic tract.

function: The label spans the hypothalamus (autonomic, endocrine, circadian and behavioral control), the subthalamus (motor control through the subthalamic nucleus and the pallidothalamic pathways), the mammillary bodies (memory), the optic tract (vision), the substantia nigra and ventral tegmental area (dopamine) and the red nucleus (cerebellar outflow); functionally it is the crossroads through which the limbic forebrain, the basal ganglia, the cerebellum and the brainstem exchange fibers with the thalamus and the cortex. Its individual components are described in their own entries; the container is useful for volumetric follow-up and as a landmark region for the thalamoperforating and anterior choroidal artery territories.

bestView.label: ventral diencephalon below the thalamus and beside the third ventricle
hypothalamus and subthalamus in front of the midbrain

imaging.normalAppearance: Gray matter beneath the thalamus and around the lower third ventricle on coronal images, extending from the chiasm to the midbrain; the FreeSurfer label includes the optic tract and the upper substantia nigra, so it is not a pure gray-matter structure.

pathology.finding: Restricted diffusion in the subthalamic-hypothalamic region with contralateral hemiballismus, hemiparesis or amnesia depending on the artery.
Mass in the ventral diencephalon with endocrine, sleep and behavioral disturbance; enhancement pattern distinguishes glioma, germinoma and hamartoma.
Symmetric FLAIR hyperintensity of the medial thalami, mammillary bodies and periventricular hypothalamus.

examination: Endocrine screen, temperature and sleep history
Movement examination for ballismus, tremor and parkinsonism
pearls: The ventral diencephalon label is a segmentation convenience; when a lesion is here, ask which of its residents is hit
Its volume shrinks in Alzheimer disease and in hypothalamic disorders and is a reproducible measure
It is the region where the anterior choroidal, thalamoperforating and posterior communicating arteries meet

pitfalls: Automated volumes of the ventral diencephalon include the optic tract and part of the midbrain; interpret changes with the anatomy in mind
